newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta softens vs mark but weakness seen contained.
newsitem.headline: Peseta softens vs mark but weakness seen contained.

text.p: The peseta, unsettled by fears of interest rate hikes in Germany, has softened against the mark, but analysts said on Tuesday they did not expect the currency to weaken much further.

"We have come from 84.20 per mark and with the correction seen in bonds and stocks, some investors are unwinding their positions, but we do not expect any major depreciation in the peseta," said Jaume Balaguer, head of the corporate desk at Banco Sabadell.
By 1350 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.53/56 per mark compared with 84.43/44 late on Monday and 84.38/40 at the end of last week.

Analysts said concerns that a firm dollar may prompt the Bundesbank to raise its repo rate have weakened the peseta along with other European currencies. Germany's Ifo institute said on Tuesday European central banks are under some pressure to raise interest rates to defend currencies.

"Certainly, there is a fear of a rate change after so many years of low interest rates in Europe, but with a more prudent monetary policy (in Spain) and the good prospects for participation in a single currency we don't really expect great fluctuations," Cesar Cantalapiedra, analyst at AFI said.

Analysts said a background of stable interest rates, good economic indicators and optimism that Spain will join Europe's single currency at its launch in 1999 would continue to provide strong support for the currency.
"The peseta cannot extract itself from the general course in the markets, but the underlying tone of the currency continues to be stable," said one dealer.

The Bank of Spain left its key money market rate unchanged at 5.25 percent on Tuesday. After a tender on Tuesday, the Bundesbank made no immediate comment on money market activities contrary to market expectations that it would announce a repo tender at a variable rate due to mark weakness.
Analysts pointed out that in recent months, the peseta has been under pressure to appreciate with the Bank of Spain appearing reluctant to cut rates further for the time being.

The central bank has intervened on a number of occasions to subdue peseta strength. Currency reserve data on Tuesday revealed that central reserves had grown in July by $1.60 billion to $68.96 billion.
Dealers believe the central bank is keen to hold the currency in a range between 84.00 and 85.00 per mark in the run-up to a single currency.
"The range of fluctuation in the coming months will continue between 84.20 and 84.70," said Balaguer.
